newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims flat in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims flat in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up for first-time unemployment benefits was unchanged last week, the government said Wednesday.
Filings for state jobless benefits stood at 342,000, unchanged from a revised level the prior week, the Labour Department said in its weekly report.
Claims in the Nov. 16 week were previously reported as 344,000.
The latest weekly total exceeded forecasts of Wall Street economists, who had predicted filings would dip to 336,000.
The four-week moving average -- viewed as a more reliable economic indicator because it smooths out weekly fluctuations -- also held steady at 336,250.
The total number of Americans on employment benefit rolls tumbled by 61,000 to 2.42 million in the week ended Nov. 16, the most recent period for which that data were available.
The Labour Department said three states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Nov. 16, the latest period for which the data were available.
They were Illinois, with 1,800; Ohio, with 1,762; and New Jersey, with 1,520.
Illinois and New Jersey reported layoffs in the trade and service industries. Illinois also had layoffs in manufacturing. Ohio said there were seasonal layoffs in various industries across the state.
Seven states reporting decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Nov. 16 week.
They were California, with 8,067; Texas, with 3,189; Louisiana, with 1,666; Washington, with 1,489; Michigan, with 1,308; Oregon, with 1,301; and Florida, with 1,261.

California cited fewer layoffs in the service industry and agriculture, while Michigan reported fewer layoffs in the auto industry. Florida said there were fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries, manufacturing and agriculture.
Texas, Louisiana, Washington and Oregon gave no explanation for their decreases, the department said.
